title: Choose the visual world for LandSetu
question: The roll assigned the Gazette Notice direction. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Gazette Notice
options.lineage: bilingual official gazettes and their notified schedules
options.thesis: Every parcel reads as a numbered notice: each value is a clause that cites the authority behind it.
options.viewport: Map framed as a notified schedule with a numbered legend in the margin; the parcel panel opens as a notice whose clauses each end in their source.
options.risk: A gazette look could be mistaken for an official notification, so it uses no emblem, no notification numbers, and a prototype masthead on every screen.

raised.raise: Each provenance colour is reserved for its one meaning and appears nowhere else in the interface.
The map carries a measured frame: scale bar, live coordinates and a grid tied to real metres.
ULPINs, areas and tax values are set in tabular figures so columns line up.
Every empty, missing and refused state is named literally, in plain words.
The ruled frame is the layout grid: map, legend and notice sit in fixed ruled bays.

regions.label: parcel notice: numbered clauses with source

options.label: Registry Stamp
options.lineage: sub-registrar and revenue office stamps, seals and initials
options.thesis: Every value carries the stamp of whoever attests it: department seal, officer initial or none.
options.viewport: Map beside a register page; each field sits on a ruled line with its stamp at the line end.
options.risk: Rubber stamps are the familiar shorthand for anything official and can slide into decoration.

options.label: Terminal Wayfinding
options.thesis: The workspace as a chain of decision points, each showing only the choices ahead.
options.viewport: A yellow band over the map naming the state and the next action.
options.case: Strong on clarity for citizens, weaker on audience identification for revenue officers.
options.risk: Saturated yellow competes with parcel colours on the map.
options.kept: One colour reserved for one meaning.

options.label: Signal Bench
options.thesis: Everything measured against a fixed graticule.
options.viewport: Parcels as traces on a dark measured grid.
options.case: Loses both axes: dark lab-bench glow reads technical, not public record.
options.risk: Neon on black is explicitly out of tone.
options.kept: A measured frame: scale and coordinates always on the map.

options.label: Datamatics Field
options.case: Loses both axes: strobing data art undermines calm legibility.

options.label: Quoted Labels
options.viewport: Quoted zone labels over the map.
options.case: Loses both axes: fashion irony is wrong for a land record.
options.kept: Plain, literal names for every state.

options.label: Elbow Panel
options.thesis: The frame itself is the layout grid.
options.case: Loses both axes: pop-culture console, pastel on black.
options.risk: Out of tone and not colourblind-safe.
options.kept: A fixed ruled frame organises the workspace.

options.label: Cloud Quarry
options.case: Loses both axes: dissolving architecture contradicts a permanent record.
options.risk: Metaphor fights the product's claim of permanence.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A GIGW-style government portal, executed with full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Blue header, service cards, map in a card.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every portal by design.
